response.question: main ekk 16 years ke larki ke saath ger sambandh karte huye pakra gaya main 15 saal ka hoon toh kya karu main
response.answer:
Mujhe samajh hai ki aap ghabraye hue honge. Aap 15 saal ke hain aur ladki 16 saal ki hai—dono bachche hain. Abhi kisi bharosemand bade vyakti aur bachchon ke mamle dekhne wale vakil se baat karein.

Di gayi jankari se yeh tay nahi kiya ja sakta ki kaunsa apradh bana hai. Agar POCSO ke tahat kisi bachche par apradh ka mamla banta hai, to usse bachchon ke liye bane Juvenile Justice Act ke tahat dekha jata hai [pocso_act_2012:34]. Juvenile Justice Board (bachchon ke mamle dekhne wala board) bachche ke liye legal aid, yani kanooni madad, ki uplabdhata sunishchit karta hai [jj_act_2015:8].

Agar police aapko pakadti hai, to kanoon ke mutabik aapko police lockup ya jail mein nahi rakha jana chahiye. Aapko bina deri ke, yatra ka samay chhodkar 24 ghante ke andar Board ke saamne pesh kiya jana chahiye [jj_act_2015:10].

Kya aapko police ne pakda hai, ya ghar walon ya kisi aur ne dekha tha? Graphic details batane ki zarurat nahi hai.

response.question: My 14-year-old son was picked up by the police for stealing a phone. Can they keep him in the police lock-up?
response.answer:
No. Your son is a child, and the police must not place him in a police lock-up or jail, even though he is accused of stealing a phone. [jj_act_2015:10]

He must be placed under the charge of the special juvenile police unit or a designated child welfare police officer. They must bring him before the Juvenile Justice Board without delay, within 24 hours of apprehension, excluding necessary travel time. [jj_act_2015:10]

The law generally provides for a child to be released on bail or placed under supervision or suitable care. There are exceptions, including where release would expose the child to danger or defeat the ends of justice. The Board must record its reasons if it denies bail. [jj_act_2015:12]

If the police do not release him on bail before he is brought before the Board, he must be kept only in an observation home or a place of safety, as applicable—not a police lock-up. [jj_act_2015:12] The Board is also responsible for ensuring that he has legal aid and that you can participate in the process. [jj_act_2015:8]

response.question: Can a newspaper print the name and photo of a 17-year-old boy accused of a crime?
response.answer:
Generally, no. A 17-year-old is a child. A child accused of an offence is covered by the protections for a child in conflict with law, if he was under 18 when the alleged offence took place. [jj_act_2015:2]

A newspaper reporting on an inquiry, investigation or court proceedings must not publish his name, photo or other details that could identify him. [jj_act_2015:74]

There is an exception: the Juvenile Justice Board or Child Welfare Committee holding the inquiry may permit disclosure if it considers this to be in the child’s best interest and records its reasons in writing. [jj_act_2015:74]

A person who breaks this prohibition can face up to six months’ imprisonment, a fine of up to ₹2 lakh, or both. [jj_act_2015:74]

response.question: Can a child who is accused of an offence get bail in India?
response.answer:
Yes. A child accused of an offence can get bail in India. When a person who is apparently a child is detained by police or brought before the Juvenile Justice Board, the law says they shall generally be released on bail, whether the alleged offence is bailable or non-bailable. Bail may be granted with or without a surety—a person who gives an assurance for the child's appearance. The child may instead be placed under the supervision of a probation officer or in the care of a suitable person. [jj_act_2015:12]

Release is not automatic in every case. It can be denied if there are reasonable grounds to believe that release is likely to bring the child into association with a known criminal, expose the child to moral, physical or psychological danger, or defeat the ends of justice. The Board must record its reasons and the circumstances for denying bail. [jj_act_2015:12]

If the police do not release the child, the child must be kept in an observation home or a place of safety until they can be brought before the Board. If the Board does not release the child, it must order placement in an observation home or a place of safety during the inquiry. [jj_act_2015:12]

If the child cannot meet the bail conditions within seven days of the bail order, the child must be brought before the Board so that the conditions can be modified. [jj_act_2015:12]
